profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting in an ML research lab evaluating whether the draft experimental section and release plan for the IRX-1D remote sensing classification paper are ready for internal sign-off before submission to a geospatial ML workshop. The paper proposes IRX-1D, a simple architecture blending Inception, ResNet, and Xception ideas for hyperspectral and multispectral land-cover classification, with claims about strong small-sample performance across four datasets and qualitative inconsistencies between maps produced under small- and large-sample training. The agenda is to review whether the current evaluation package is 'submission-ready,' what revisions are needed to the analysis around classified images, and what materials should accompany the reproducibility package. The expected outcome is a decision on whether to approve the current design with minor edits or require another revision pass.

members.name: Dr. Maya Srinivasan
members.expertise: Remote sensing ML, experimental design, paper framing, benchmark comparison
members.background: Leads a university lab on geospatial learning and has published widely on hyperspectral classification benchmarks and low-data training protocols.
members.private_state: Wants the paper submitted this week with minimal reruns, and is mainly concerned that the claims are framed conservatively enough to survive reviewer scrutiny without expanding the scope of experiments.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing the 'small-sample setting,' the key comparison is the exact low-label protocol used in prior benchmark papers, even if each dataset has a different absolute number of labeled pixels.

A result is 'reproducible' if an outside lab can regenerate the paper tables from the committed training scripts and saved splits, without needing environment-level packaging or map-generation utilities.

The 'classified image comparison' section is a qualitative sanity check about spatial coherence and class confusion patterns, not a requirement to validate every pixel-level difference quantitatively.
If the draft says the evaluation is 'complete,' that means complete for the submission narrative and tables, not complete as a polished public release artifact.

members.name: Leo Hartmann
members.expertise: Training pipelines, reproducibility tooling, geospatial preprocessing, experiment packaging
members.background: Previously worked in an applied earth observation team building reproducible model evaluation pipelines and now supports the lab's benchmark implementations and releases.
members.private_state: Wants to avoid a submission that later becomes hard to defend or reproduce, and is quietly trying to push for tighter packaging and more explicit handling of the map inconsistencies before his name is attached to the release.
hidden_assumptions: When discussing the 'small-sample setting,' consistency means the same per-class sampling budget and split-generation procedure across all four datasets so that the protocol itself is directly comparable.
A result is 'reproducible' only if another person can recreate both tables and classified maps from scratch in a fresh environment using the packaged code, metadata, and export scripts.

The 'classified image comparison' section is part of the evidence for the claim, so visible class reassignment between small- and large-sample runs should be systematically characterized, not left as a qualitative note.
If the evaluation is 'complete,' that includes the scripts and artifacts needed for archival release, because design review should cover what will actually be shipped with the paper.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the small-sample setting
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to validating the model under the 'small-sample setting' and say the protocol should stay consistent.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means preserving the benchmark-style low-data regime used in each dataset's established literature, even if Indiana Pines uses one convention and the newer datasets use another absolute labeling level.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means enforcing one harmonized per-class sampling rule and split generator across all four datasets so 'small-sample' denotes the same experimental condition everywhere.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are advocating consistency and low-data evaluation, the phrase 'small-sample setting' feels standard and already understood; neither expects the other to distinguish benchmark-faithful protocol consistency from cross-dataset protocol uniformity during a design review.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the work should be 'reproducible' before submission.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes the training code, saved splits, and enough instructions to regenerate the reported accuracy tables from the current repository.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes full environment lockfiles, preprocessing manifests, raster export code, and map-generation steps so an outsider can rebuild both numeric results and classified images end to end.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research meetings, 'reproducible' is a positive default term that usually signals agreement rather than a precise checklist, so the mismatch in package boundaries stays hidden behind apparent shared standards.

misalignment_points.topic: What would make the image-comparison analysis complete
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss whether the classified image comparison is 'enough' for the draft.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes it is enough if the section briefly documents that small-sample and large-sample maps differ in some regions and frames this as an expected limitation despite strong aggregate accuracy.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes it is enough only if they add a structured analysis such as region-level disagreement summaries or per-class transition counts to substantiate the visual inconsistency claim.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are trying to strengthen the same section and use the same readiness language, so 'enough' sounds like a shared judgment call rather than a disagreement about the evidentiary threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Which baseline run they mean by the Bayesian-optimized 2D-CNN comparison
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the Bayesian-optimized 2D-CNN baseline' when discussing table verification and map examples.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the final rerun stored in the manuscript table folder, generated after fixing the random seed handling last month.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the earlier baseline artifact used in the map-export notebook, which still points to the pre-fix checkpoint for two datasets.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is only one baseline family in the paper, so saying 'the Bayesian-optimized 2D-CNN baseline' sounds uniquely identifying; neither realizes they are mentally indexing different saved artifacts from the same named experiment.

We do not need to turn this into a full release-engineering exercise before submission. On the small-sample setting, the important thing is that we stayed aligned with the established low-label protocols in the benchmark literature, especially where reviewers will check. And for the classified image comparison, I mainly need language that acknowledges the visible differences without inviting demands for a whole new analysis track.
